practice.q: Despite frozen bilateral ties, India continues to engage Pakistan through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). Discuss the significance of such multilateral engagement for India.
parts: Introduction: tensions with Pakistan, yet engagement through the SCO
India's engagement with Pakistan at the SCO (multi-dimensional)
Significance of multilateral engagement for India: positives (multi-dimensional)
Way forward with conclusion (10 marks, so combined)

answer.t: India–Pakistan ties have been frozen over cross-border terrorism, from Pathankot and Uri (2016) to Pahalgam (2025). Yet India still engages Pakistan at the SCO, most recently inviting its culture minister to the Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi (Nov 2026).

answer.h: How India engages Pakistan through the SCO

pts.t: An SCO host must invite all members, so engagement follows the rules of the grouping rather than signalling a thaw.
Ministers meet at SCO events even when bilateral visits are off.
pts.ex: Bilawal Bhutto in Goa, 2023; Jaishankar in Islamabad, 2024.

pts.t: Both sit in the SCO's counter-terror framework, where India can press its concerns on terror.
Pakistan lies on India's shortest land route to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
pts.ex: India flagged 'connectivity, transit and trade' in Islamabad, 2026.

pts.t: The SCO keeps regional trade on the agenda while bilateral trade is suspended.
A low-risk track built on shared heritage, not disputed politics.
pts.ex: Civilisational Dialogue proposed by PM Modi at Tianjin, 2025.

answer.h: Significance of multilateral engagement for India

pts.t: India stays firm on terror without looking isolationist or blocking regional cooperation.
The SCO balances India's partnerships with the West (Quad) with a seat among Russia, China and Central Asia.
Multilateral forums let India put cross-border terror before Pakistan's partners.
Central Asia offers energy and markets; the SCO complements routes such as INSTC and Chabahar.
Proposing and hosting initiatives lets India set the agenda instead of reacting.
Civilisational diplomacy projects India's cultural depth and builds goodwill beyond governments.
China's weight and closeness to Pakistan can tilt SCO positions against India's interests.
pts.ex: India's opposition to CPEC through PoK.

pts.t: Hostile members dilute joint positions, so results stay on paper.
pts.ex: India declined the SCO Defence Ministers' statement in June 2025 as it omitted Pahalgam.

answer.t: India should use the SCO to keep terror on the agenda, advance connectivity and culture where interests meet, and tie any bilateral step to verifiable action against terror. Done this way, multilateral engagement lets India stay firm on security and present in Eurasia: principle and pragmatism together.

trend.t: UPSC has moved from India–Pakistan as a bilateral question (soft power, 2015) to the regional groupings that frame it: SAARC stalled by terror (2016), the SCO asked twice in three years (2021, 2023) and Central Asia connectivity (2018, 2024). The newer questions ask about India's role, not just facts about the grouping.
